newsitem.title: USA: US debt allocations shift in Oct 1 week - survey.
newsitem.headline: US debt allocations shift in Oct 1 week - survey.

text.p: Money managers shifted their U.S. debt allocations in the week following the Federal Reserve's decision to keep monetary policy steady, said a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates Inc.
The Fed's decision to hold a steady monetary policy last week may have had an influence on money manager decisions and portfolio structure, said a report on the survey.
"The data suggests that there has been solid money manager participation in the rally that has ensued the (Federal Open Market Committee) policy decision," the report said.
In the week ended October 1, the survey's bear/bull index arithmetic reading rose to 4.36, while the asset-weighted number jumped to 4.39, up from 4.02 in the previous period, according the report.
A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating investors are mostly long on the market.
The cash/assets ratio fell to 7.06 percent from 7.18 percent.
Duration bogey held steady at 4.06 on an arithmetic basis and 4.69 on a weighted basis.
Duration bogey is the level of asset or liability duration sought in the management of a portfolio.
Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.

Four percent of the portfolio managers polled said they were planning to be active in the coming week, down from 12 percent the week before. The bear/bull index collected among those intending to be active was 5.0, up from 4.0 the previous week.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
